description: Daily credit budgets, rollover behavior, balance visibility, and observed costs for the cloud music providers used with the studio. Grounds generation strategy: spend scarce credits only on near-final prompts.

happyshrimp_10.label: HappyShrimp 1.0 (Alibaba, beta)
happyshrimp_10.observed_cost: Results usually extremely good, but the daily allowance is tiny and leftovers are wiped at the next day's reset, like Suno. Unlike Suno it DOES show the remaining credit amount.
happyshrimp_10.strategy: Scarcest resource: check the visible balance first, spend only on near-final prompts. Use-it-or-lose-it daily — plan the day's generations up front.

lyria_35.label: Google Lyria 3.5 (Flow Music)
lyria_35.observed_cost: No charge or balance shown on the free plan. Flow clamps requested durations (4:06 requested -> 3:00; player showed 2:56).
lyria_35.strategy: Pronunciation is the weak spot — finalize lyric singability on Suno v6-mini before spending Flow runs. Request longer than needed; expect clamping.

minimax_30.label: MiniMax Music 3.0
minimax_30.observed_cost: 300 credits per song on the web form (600 at the default quantity of 2). An 8,800-point free balance was observed Sep 2026.
minimax_30.strategy: Best home for multi-variant comparisons and A/B tests — batch generations here, not on Suno or HappyShrimp.

suno_v6.label: Suno v6
suno_v6.observed_cost: 50 credits/day on the free plan; no balance display anywhere in the current web UI (checked Sep 2026); no carryover — unused credits vanish at reset.
suno_v6.strategy: Sketch on v6-mini (pronounces cleanest, cheap iterations), run keepers on v6 flagship. Never burn agent time re-checking for a balance display — it does not exist.

title: Cloud music provider credit economics
